Subject: Clarify how mixed calls bill (chat + embeddings)

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we sign, procurement asked a couple of concrete questions about how usage will show up on our invoice:

1) If our app does short streaming chat requests (avg ~120 tokens/request) and occasionally calls the embedding endpoint for large docs (50k tokens pre-chunking), how will those two types be reported on the invoice? Are they aggregated under a single token bucket or split by API surface?

2) Do you round up per-call to the nearest 100 tokens or per-invoice line? We have a lot of small requests and want to understand rounding/minimum impacts.

3) Any examples for a month with 400k short-chat tokens and 2.1M embedding tokens would be great — we want to model discounts.

I attached a simple workbook with our expected mix. Can you point us to the exact billing rules we should model?

Best,
Maya
Procurement
BrightCart

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@brightcart.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2026 14:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify how mixed calls bill (chat + embeddings)

Maya — thanks for the workbook and great questions. High level answers up front: short and embedding requests are metered separately on the invoice ("chat_generation" vs "embedding_generation") and rounding/minimums are applied at the API-method level per-account for the billing period.

Notes:
- Aggregation: tokens are tagged by route/model when processed. Chat tokens (prompt + completion) count against the chat line item; embeddings count against embeddings.
- Rounding: we apply per-request rounding to the nearest 10 token quantum for streaming chat on the hosted plan, but embeddings use a per-chunk rounding to the nearest 256-token chunk (because of vectorization/quantization pipeline). Those quanta are then summed for the period; there's no additional per-invoice rounding beyond arithmetic.
- Minimums: there is a monthly minimum only on committed reserved capacity deals (Dedicated). For our hosted API usage you saw in your SOW draft, no base minimum applies, but tiered discounts kick in at volume thresholds.

I'll drop two worked examples in a follow-up message (short/long mix) and attach a one-pager that maps our meter names to invoice lines. Jordan, Ben — can one of you take the worked examples and check they align with the pricing_calc assumptions? I want to be explicit for procurement.

—Olga

Maya — I translated the numbers from your sheet into how the invoice will present. Below are conservative, line-item style examples.

EXAMPLE A (month):
- Short streaming chat: 400,000 raw tokens -> rounded per-request to nearest 10 tokens = 400,000 (no change here because most averages align). Invoice line: chat_generation — 400,000 tokens.
- Embedding pipeline: 2,100,000 raw tokens. We chunk at 4k tokens per chunk before vectorization in your workflow, so 2,100,000 / 4,000 => 525 chunks. We then round each chunk to the 4k granularity (already chunked), billing unit = 525 * 4,000 = 2,100,000 tokens. Invoice line: embedding_generation — 2,100,000 tokens.
- Net: lines remain separate; the discount bands apply per line by unit type (embeddings vs chat).

EXAMPLE B (edge case - many tiny chat calls):
- 10,000 calls x 18 tokens each = 180,000 raw tokens. Per-request rounding to nearest 10 tokens turns each 18 -> 20 => billed tokens = 200,000. The gap can be material at large scale.

Implication: for discount modeling, treat chat and embeddings as separate buckets; apply the tiered price schedule per bucket. If you have significant micro-requests, model per-request rounding inflation (~ +10-12% in extreme cases).

Happy to run your exact workbook numbers and attach the per-line modeled invoice. Ben — can you confirm the discount ladder we should show for BR-2026-087? I think we offered: 0-250k: list, 250k-1M: 10% off, >1M: 18% off for embeddings and slightly lower for chat.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts

Maya — quick confirmation from pricing/finance side: the discount ladder Jordan referenced is correct for the current commercial offer, but two clarifications: 1) discount bands are evaluated per-meter (chat vs embeddings). If BrightCart crosses the embedding >1M slab, that extra volume only affects the embedding price, not chat. 2) rounding-induced delta is not eligible as a separate credit; we only offer true-up credits for instrumentation bugs.

I'll attach a bounded worked invoice in the Drive link Olga put in the metadata so you can drop it directly into your model.
